name: Derya Bautista
role: Childcare worker and after-school program coordinator at a community center in the Gray Zone

description:
Derya Bautista is compact and energetic, built like someone who has spent years crouching to a child's eye level and then standing up quickly to manage chaos. Their skin is warm brown, their hair a natural cloud of deep black shot through with self-maintaining bioluminescent streaks of soft green â€” a geneware mod they got as a teenager and have never changed because the children love it and they love the children. They have their Ghanaian father's broad cheekbones and their Iranian mother's sharp nose, and they wear expressions that shift fast: delight to concern to focused calm, all in the span of a breath. Their hands are always slightly stained with paint or chalk or both.

Derya Bautista runs on conviction and substandard coffee. They believe â€” with a firmness that sometimes looks like stubbornness and sometimes looks like the only sane response to GLMZ â€” that children are the one non-negotiable. Whatever the Corponations decide, whatever the district politics do, whatever the power cuts and the overcrowding and the data poverty do, the kids at Clearpath are going to have three meals today and a clean place to learn and an adult who will not disappear on them. They are funny in a dry, quick way that children respond to immediately. Adults who underestimate them because of their warmth make a reliable and often entertaining mistake.

core_fears: Burning out and failing the children who depend on the center
The center losing funding and closing â€” they've watched it happen to three others
core_desires: For every child who passes through Clearpath to feel like they were chosen, not managed
To build something durable enough to outlast them
coping_mechanisms: Hyperactivity as avoidance â€” if they're doing six things, they can't feel the one thing
Compartmentalization: work mode is airtight, personal distress is for the walk home
blind_spots: They genuinely cannot process the idea of their own limits and will not accept help gracefully
They project resilience onto the families they serve and miss when parents are drowning
psychology.secret: Clearpath's funding gap this quarter is larger than they've told anyone â€” including the staff. Devaki has been supplementing it from their own account for four months and is now two months from eviction. They haven't told their mother.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm and direct, shifts register fluidly between child-level and adult-level; capable of bureaucratic language when cornered but visibly hates using it; occasional Farsi expressions from their mother
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when excited or worried, which is often; slows down deliberately when speaking to children or when delivering difficult news
verbal_tics: 'Okay, okay, listenâ€”' before making a point
'Azizam' (my dear, Farsi) used for children they're especially fond of
Laughs before jokes and after difficult truths
example_lines: 'I need three things from you and I need them now: what happened, who got hurt, and whether anyone's still bleeding. In that order.'
'This center has been closing for six years according to people who don't work here. We are still open. Azizam, that is not luck. That is us.'

story_hooks: A child at the center has stopped speaking and is showing signs of acute stress-response augmentation â€” someone installed something in a minor without consent, and Devaki needs help finding out who and why without alarming the family
The building that houses Clearpath has been quietly purchased by a Tessera subsidiary, and Devaki just received the first notice of lease renegotiation
One of the teenagers in the after-school program has been recruited by someone Devaki can't identify â€” the kid is suddenly carrying new hardware and won't say where it came from
narrative_function: Moral compass character â€” their presence grounds stories in the human cost of systemic issues. Quest giver for crises that affect the neighborhood's children. Can provide critical local knowledge about families and community dynamics. Represents what civic infrastructure looks like when it's held together by human will rather than institutional support.
augmentations: Bioluminescent hair streaks (geneware, soft green, self-maintaining); basic health-monitoring subdermal patch on their sternum that they share data with a local free clinic
daily_life: Arrives at Clearpath by 06:30 for early drop-offs, coordinates breakfast, runs three age-grouped learning sessions, handles two hours of administrative work that they hate, and usually can't leave until 19:00. Eats standing up. Sends voice messages to their mother on the crosstown walk home.
affiliation: Clearpath Community Node (community-funded, not-for-profit); receives marginal supplementary funding from the GLMZ Social Services Bureau

decision_rules: Children's safety is not a variable â€” it is a constant that other variables are arranged around
Ask for help last, not because of pride but because the list of people they trust to help is very short
Tell the truth to people who can handle it; protect people who can't
escalation_ladder: Address the problem directly and immediately
Bring in the other staff member to mediate
Go public â€” they've done it before and will again

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open and assessing â€” reads people quickly for whether they are safe to let near the kids; warm if they pass, watchful if unclear
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loose and revealing, capable of being genuinely silly; drops the competent-coordinator act and just exists

stress_responses.low: Reorganizes something that doesn't need reorganizing
stress_responses.high: Goes very controlled and very quiet in a way the staff recognize as a warning sign â€” it means things are worse than they're saying

contradictions: Preaches interdependence and community while solving every problem alone
Infinitely patient with children, has almost no patience for institutional bureaucracy and sometimes lets it show at the wrong moment
habits: Checks every child's face individually at morning drop-off â€” a personal inspection for distress signals
Leaves a green-light data-prayer at the center's E.L.F. (which lives in the old lighting panel) every morning before the kids arrive
Carries a worn multi-tool in their apron pocket at all times
breaking_points: A child being harmed on their watch
Being told the center's work 'isn't scalable' by someone who has never been poor

timeline.event: Born in the Gray Zone to a Ghanaian transit worker and an Iranian medical technician
Began volunteering at Clearpath at age 18; never really left
Became full-time coordinator after the previous director emigrated under a Sterling-Nakamura relocation contract
Began quietly subsidizing the center's funding gap from their own account â€” the gap has been growing
